text: X numerical input data data.frame, matrix tibble format. alpha level significance. Default 0.01. 1/100 chance point falsely classified outlier. beta quantile threshold used GPD estimation. Default 0.90. ensure enough data available, values greater 0.90 set 0.90. gamma quantile minimum spanning tree edge lengths used compute bandwidth. Default 0.98. Ignored bw provided, ignored old_version = TRUE, largest gap consecutive edge lengths used instead. See Details. bw support radius Epanechnikov kernel, scale data scaling. NULL (default), computed minimum spanning tree data described Details. gpd Generalized Pareto distribution parameters. NULL (default), estimated data. scale TRUE (default), data scaled bandwidth density estimates computed: mvscale() old_version = FALSE, columns approximately uncorrelated unit scale, scaling column range [0, 1] old_version = TRUE. fast TRUE, kernel density estimate sum k nearest neighbours point , including point , k = min(max(ceiling(n / 200), 100), n, 500) n = NROW(X); k 100 500, equals 100 whenever 100 <= n <= 20000. Wherever k - 1 observations lie inside kernel support, typical bulk data three dimensions, sum truncated estimate lower exact one. Sparse observations, candidates outliers, fewer k neighbours inside support estimates unchanged, although GPD threshold fit can still differ. FALSE, kernel summed exactly observations inside support, found fixed-radius search (frNN()). time memory exact computation proportional number pairs observations within bw . two dimensions usually modest, three dimensions kernel support bulk data can contain thousands observations, exact computation still order n^2 worst case fast = TRUE remains practical choice large n. Default TRUE NROW(X) > 10000. bandwidth calculation always uses data. old_version TRUE, algorithm Kandanaarachchi Hyndman (2022) used. Default FALSE, giving algorithm Hyndman, Kandanaarachchi Turner (2026). See Details.

title: Identifies outliers using the algorithm lookout. — lookout
text: list following components: data input data X, scaling. outliers set outliers. outlier_probability GPD probability data. outlier_scores outlier scores data. bandwidth support radius Epanechnikov kernel: either bw, value computed minimum spanning tree multiplied sqrt(NCOL(X) + 4). kde kernel density estimate values. lookde leave-one-kde values. gpd fitted GPD parameters. call matched call.

title: Identifies outliers using the algorithm lookout. — lookout
text: algorithm three steps. Scaling. scale = TRUE, data first scaled mvscale(): column centred median, data rotated scaled using Cholesky factor inverse robust (MCD) covariance estimate, columns approximately uncorrelated unit scale. Leave-one-density estimates. kernel density estimate computed observation using spherically symmetric Epanechnikov kernel support radius bw, contribution observation removed give leave-one-estimate. bw = NULL, bandwidth computed Euclidean minimum spanning tree (scaled) data find_tda_bw(): gamma quantile (type 8) tree's edge lengths multiplied sqrt(m + 4), m = NCOL(X). spherically symmetric Epanechnikov kernel support radius h m dimensions standard deviation h / sqrt(m + 4) coordinate, scaling makes kernel's per-coordinate standard deviation equal quantile. fast = TRUE, kernel summed k nearest neighbours point ; see fast argument. Extreme value model. negative logarithms density estimates (surprisals) beta quantile modelled generalized Pareto distribution (GPD), fitted maximum likelihood using fpot(). surprisals bounded, shape parameter constrained zero: unconstrained estimate positive, GPD refitted shape fixed zero. fitted GPD gives, observation, probability leave-one-surprisal least large one observed, multiplied 1 - beta. Observations whose probability alpha declared outliers. Setting old_version = TRUE gives algorithm Kandanaarachchi Hyndman (2022) instead. differs three places: data scaled column lies [0, 1], rather mvscale(); bandwidth lower end largest gap consecutive minimum spanning tree edge lengths among median, rather gamma quantile, multiplied sqrt(m + 4); GPD shape parameter constrained.

title: lookout (development version)
text: exact density estimates (fast = FALSE) now use fixed-radius neighbour search via dbscan::frNN(), memory longer grows NROW(X)^2. Results unchanged rounding. Nearest neighbour searches now use dbscan rather RANN, longer imported. default now fast = NROW(X) > 10000. lookout() gives helpful error GPD fitted many observations neighbours within bandwidth. mvscale() now matches weird::mvscale(), robust MCD covariance estimate default. changes scaled data used lookout() persisting_outliers() scale = TRUE. Fixed Epanechnikov kernel scaling multivariate data. fast argument find_tda_bw() deprecated ignored. Now requires R >= 4.1.0. Bug fixes documentation improvements.
